fields.title: Not Collecting Is Also a Decision
fields.keyTakeaway: Every field is a liability, not an asset, and a field audit usually shows that a third of them are not used by any feature.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The "date of birth" field in the profile. Is it needed?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Data is perceived as a free asset: collected just in case, maybe it will come in handy. In reality, each field is a liability: store, protect, delete upon request, explain to the regulator. Half of the fields in a typical product are never used.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: **[[data-minimisation|Data minimization]]** — collect and store only what is necessary for the stated purpose. This is simultaneously a legal requirement in most jurisdictions and a practical risk-reduction principle.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: Four questions before adding a field:
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **For what specific purpose?** Not "for personalization", but "to congratulate on a birthday". If there is no specific purpose — there is no field.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Can we make do with less precise data?** Birth year instead of date. City instead of address. Age group instead of age. Usually yes, and risk drops significantly.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Can it be computed instead of stored?** Age is computed from year. Buyer category — from history.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **What happens if this field is not there?** Often nothing.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **[[purpose-limitation|Purpose limitation]]** — the second principle: data collected for one purpose is not used for another without a new legal basis. An address collected for delivery cannot become the basis for ad targeting.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Separately about **geolocation precision**: the difference between a city, a neighborhood, and a point on the map is the difference between regular and sensitive data. A person's exact trajectory reveals where they live, work, and their habits.
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: A practical technique — **field audit**: go through all stored fields and name the feature using each. Fields without a feature are deleted.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: An audit of profile fields produced a result typical for products of this age:
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/rows/4/2: Kept, retention period 30 days after delivery
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Four fields out of seven deleted. Not a single feature suffered — they were collected "for the future" that never arrived.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Exact coordinates — a separate decision: they are needed by the courier at the time of delivery and not needed afterwards. Retention period 30 days instead of indefinite.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Geolocation when choosing a store: first requested exact position, then — only for determining nearest stores, with rounding to the neighborhood when saving. Selection precision didn't change, data sensitivity dropped.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Minimization conflicts with analytics and machine learning, which find data useful. Resolved through aggregation and anonymization — the next node.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Every field is a liability, not an asset, and a field audit usually shows that a third of them are not used by any feature.
